description: The Global Assessment Report on Disaster Risk Reduction 2015 (GAR15) produced a global probabilistic risk model, and UNDRR publishes its inputs and results on the Humanitarian Data Exchange. The exposure layer comes as 181 country datasets (found by name on 2026-09-26): a top-down database in which national statistics on socio-economics, building type and capital stock are spread onto 5 x 5 km or 1 x 1 km grids using population and GDP as proxies. Hazard layers include a global tropical cyclone wind model for 50, 100, 250, 500 and 1,000-year return periods, built from 2,594 historical cyclones, topography, roughness and bathymetry, and a tsunami run-up model for a 500-year return period. Results include multi-hazard average annual loss per country, the long-term expected yearly loss, and a volcano population exposure index supplied by Global Volcano Model and IAVCEI. Coverage: global, as of 2015. Access: zipped shapefiles, grids and a results workbook, with metadata PDFs inside the archives. Licence: listed on HDX as 'other', with terms in each dataset; free. Caveats: UNDRR states the data come from global datasets, should be read as orders of magnitude, and must not be used for local planning or life-saving decisions; the model has not been updated since 2015. Simulation uses are global exposure and hazard inputs for screening building and facility risk and for comparing national loss estimates. Related records: the DesInventar Sendai loss databases and the multi-hazard vulnerability database.
